subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an internal `rescueWatchdog` cron payload that can probe, restart, and run doctor repair for another managed profile after it is rebased onto the current cron protocol/store/runtime?
rationale: The branch adds a new unattended recovery capability across cron, gateway, service control, and doctor repair; automation can find stale-base defects, but it cannot choose the permanent core security/product boundary or accept the operator risk.

options.title: Sponsor after rebase and proof
options.body: Keep the PR open, require the current-main protocol/store/command compatibility repair, and ask for real-host recovery proof plus secops/product review before merge.

options.title: Move to external/plugin path
options.body: Decline the core cron payload for now and keep recovery as an external watchdog or plugin-style integration until a smaller core API is approved.

options.title: Close and track the design issue
options.body: Close this stale branch and use the open Gateway resilience issue as the canonical product discussion if maintainers do not want to sponsor the current implementation path.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after rebase and proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, require the current-main protocol/store/command compatibility repair, and ask for real-host recovery proof plus secops/product review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The most consequential unresolved decision is the security boundary around unattended service restart and doctor repair, and CODEOWNERS routes part of the touched cron service surface to secops.
